utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The accused may be seated, and good morning. Good morning, ladies and gentlemen; good morning to our technicians; good morning, interpreters. I hope that they are here. Yes, I can hear you too. Good morning, court reporters, legal assistants; good morning, counsel for the Prosecution. For the record, it appears that Mr. Michael Keegan is not here today, but the Prosecution is represented by Ms. Hollis. Good morning, counsel for the Defence. I don't see Mr. Tosic here in the courtroom. Mr. Stojanovic is there, however.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you're right, Your Honour. The accused Mr. Zigic will be represented by myself only today. My name is Slobodan Stojanovic, I'm an attorney at law from Belgrade, and I have been authorised by Mr. Tosic to present his excuses today. He's absent for family reasons. But we have been preparing ourselves together, and I can guarantee that his absence will in no way be any obstacle for our normal work today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Stojanovic. We will resume the hearing of the Kvocka and others case. Let me just remind you, Ms. Hollis, that we will be working until 11.00, more or less, so if you can please indicate to me when a convenient time for a break is for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness is now being brought in.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the reason I'm on my feet, I realise it's cross-examination, but because of the difficulties we've had with the camera, the Prosecution has provided an exhibit we believe will assist the Court in terms of what rooms the witnesses are pointing to. We have an exhibit that is basically a plan of the restaurant or administration building and the hangar, both the ground floor and the first floor, with the numbers marked as they appear on the model. I've provided copies to each of the Defence teams, and at this time I'd like to offer it into evidence. I believe it would be helpful for the Court. I believe it would be next in order which is 3/77, and it would be 3/77A for the ground floor of the administration building; B for the first floor of the administration building; C for the ground floor of the hangar building; and D for the first floor of the hangar building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are there any objections, Mr. Simic, on behalf of the Defence as regards the tendering of this exhibit? MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. We do not have any objections, and I am speaking on behalf of the Defence team as a whole.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Simic. You have chosen the right place to conduct your cross-examination. I think you will be able to communicate better with the witness. Mr. O'Sullivan, you would like to say something.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Yes. Could we have someone from the technical group come and connect our LiveNote. The examination can start while this happens, but our LiveNote is not connected and we don't have the transcript. So could someone come out now and do this while the cross-examination proceeds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will take this opportunity to tell you that very often there are some minor errors in the transcript, and in order to avoid interruptions, I have to tell you that the transcripts are reviewed later on by the court reporters at least three times, so the corrections are subsequently made. It is not necessary to interrupt with questions and remarks as regards the transcript because it always gets revised after the hearing, and as far as I know, at least three times. However, if you really think that there has been a significant and important mistake, you should draw our attention to that. Mr. O'Sullivan, has the problem been solved?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: The problem seems to be on all the computers, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It should be worth mentioning that we have to check technical matters before the beginning of the hearing. The Judges are always here at 9.30 and sometimes we have to wait for a technical problem to be solved. I think that the material -- that the technical equipment should be checked beforehand, or if possible on the eve of the hearing, the night before. Could we proceed, Mr. Dubuisson? Is everything okay?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It seems that things are functioning now. Mr. Simic, I will now give you the floor so that you can continue your cross-examination. Let me just remind the witness that he's still testifying under oath and that he will now continue answering questions that will be put to him by the Defence counsel. Are you comfortable, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Mr. Simic, you have the floor. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. K. Simic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Beganovic.

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us continue where we stopped yesterday. But before we do so, I should like to ask you to provide brief answers to my questions, and I will do my best to phrase them according to the suggestion by Ms. Hollis. Let us try to have yes or no answers because in this manner we will be able to proceed in an expeditious manner, and I will get precise answers to my questions. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday, we talked about the seizure of your weapon in 1988.

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I asked you whether you knew what the word "Kratez" meant. So let me please quote your statement of the 14th and 15th of December, 1994 and the 18th of January, 1995. "My father was a hunter. When he died, he left behind two rifles; one was a 12-calibre shotgun, a so-called Kratez ..."

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There must be a technical error. That has nothing to do with my statement. First of all, the word "Kratez", I heard it yesterday for the first time from you here in the courtroom. And then the rifles were normal rifles. There was one shotgun and a carbine with a sniper. I don't know. There may have been an error in translation when it comes to this word "Kratez", I don't know what it means.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This statement was signed by you, but we will finish with the subject shortly. Let us go on. Yesterday you stated that you were not able to obtain the weapon permit because you were a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that Serbs, including Rajko Zigic, refused you the permit, but that is not important. How was it possible for your father, who was also a Muslim, to obtain in a legal manner, permits for those weapons?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I was a child.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, I will quote from your statement. "The refusal for the issuance of the weapons permit --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Excuse me. Your father lived under Yugoslavia when it was united, when he got the permit, so it was another Yugoslavia. Thank you. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I will follow up on what you have just said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your weapon was seized from you. When did it happen? Did it happen during the time of some other Yugoslavia in 1988?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was already a different kind of Yugoslavia because Tito had died. He died in 1980 so the country changed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us go back to the weapon permit. As regards the reason, the grounds for the refusal of the permit, was it not the fact stated by you in your statement that is the fact as a child, as an adolescent you had some problems regarding your behaviour?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, why would my wife also be refused the weapon permit as well?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of problems with behaviour did you have?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, how would I know? They wrote down whatever they wanted to write down. They drew a certain picture of me and this is what they did. This is what the system was like. The ethnic background did not matter. This had to do with the kind of system that was -- with the kind of authority that was in power at that time. It was during the communism.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Beganovic, we are not talking about communism, we're talking about misbehaviour during your young age as a child, as a young man, a minor person, you misbehaved. What kind of behaviour was it?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well I behaved the way I could. I don't know what kind of behaviour they had in mind. They wrote down whatever they wanted to write down in that paper.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Beganovic, I'm not asking you to tell me exactly what they wrote down on that paper. You stated in your statement that you had had certain minor problems, minor conflicts with the members of the police while you were a young man. And you also stated that your weapons were confiscated as a result of a conflict with authorities and the police.

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's a fact. And that is why the weapons were seized, but I had had those weapons for about four or five years and nobody touched them, nobody questioned the issue of inheritance because I had inherited those weapons from my father.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Beganovic, let us not go back to that, we discussed it yesterday.

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but the fact remains that Grozdanic and others from the SUP came to my house and confiscated the weapons, and this was stated in my statement of 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So because of the conflict --

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because of the conflict. That was the only reason.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you threaten anyone with those weapons?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I took those weapons maybe two or three times, otherwise I never touched them. I never fired a single bullet from those weapons. I would only clean them from time to time. I did not posses them illegally, and I did not use those hunting weapons in an active manner in any way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As regards the conflict with the Grozdanic brothers --

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- you stated explicitly that that criminal investigation was never instituted against you in any way before the hostilities?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was charged at one point but nothing was ever proved. And as regards my criminal record, I didn't have any problems.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me quote your -- what you say about that in your statement. "As far as I know, I was never investigated. I was never arrested. I was never detained. I was never convicted for any criminal activity before the outbreak of the hostilities." You gave this statement under oath. However, Mr. Beganovic, it seems that you were registered as a pickpocket?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I was taken into custody by police but I was never charged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Beganovic, it seems that we don't understand each other. We're talking at cross-purposes. I'm asking you, did you have any criminal record with the police as a pickpocket?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what I mean by the word pickpocket?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's a kind of jargon for theft.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of theft are we talking about, Mr. Beganovic?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pickpocketing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you describe it for us, please?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how to describe it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Beganovic, were you ever convicted by a final judgement of a court, and I'm referring to the municipal court in Prijedor, judgement number K706/74 dated 13th of April, 1976 because you had committed a criminal act, a criminal offence as described in Article 249(1) of the Criminal Code, the criminal offence in question being pickpocketing. Were you not convicted to spend eight months in prison plus two years on parole?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where, in Prijedor? I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you convicted or not?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean for pickpocketing? No, that has nothing to do with me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Beganovic, you're testifying under an oath.

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I am testifying under an oath but this is not correct. This is not accurate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well then. Let us go on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Simic, instead of asking the witness if he was convicted on the basis of a certain article, maybe you should phrase your question in a different way. Maybe the witness is not familiar with the relevant article. Perhaps you should ask a yes or no question and you will get your answer. Perhaps you should ask him whether he did indeed commit this offence or not. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] I will do that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you commit a criminal offence of pickpocketing?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you convicted for the said criminal offence?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't understand this thing about criminal offence. I did not commit any criminal offence in 1976. I had just finished my military service. I don't know where you got this from. I really don't understand what you're trying to say with this. Like yesterday, you accused me of cursing, but I didn't do that so you are continuing along the same line. You are accusing people for what they have never done. It's the same thing like in the Omarska camp, the Defence doing exactly the same thing that those people did in Omarska. It's all under duress. It's --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Beganovic, this is just hatred talking.

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not hatred talking from me. You are just acting like you did during the communist regime, the same Serb communist manner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, maybe the witness does not know what is provided for in Article 249(1). As far as I understand, the criminal offence in question refers to pickpocketing. So, Witness, could you please answer the question that has been put to you by Defence counsel and I have to ask you not to change roles here. Your duty is to answer questions put to you by the Defence counsel. If you don't know the answer to the question, you just say, "I don't know." Mr. Simic, please, ask your questions and do not argue with the witness. Try to ask your questions in a precise and clear manner and you will receive your answer. The answer can be yes, no, or I don't know. So let us go back to the Article 249. The offence described is pickpocketing and the question is: Were you or were you not convicted for this particular criminal offence by the municipal court in Prijedor? Could you answer that question, Witness? Were you convicted for that criminal offence or not?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Prijedor, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Simic, you have the answer, so please continue. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. President. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Beganovic, between 1977 and 1980, were you ever convicted for a criminal offence concealing and handling stolen goods by the court in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Beganovic. Do you know where the court in Zagreb is located, the so-called Peace Palace?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you ever convicted in Zagreb for any criminal offence?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Because I did not have a train ticket on a train journey so they accused me of something, but nothing was ever proved. You're bringing up things that have nothing to do with honesty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, and now, you say that there indeed has been a legal proceedings against you in Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know what I did. I was travelling on a train. I did not have a valid ticket. They called the police and they accused me of something which they never managed to prove. Please, give me some proofs and then present them to this Chamber. What about these people here? Have they been convicted?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This need not interest you at the moment, Mr. Beganovic. Let me go back to my question. Were you convicted for pickpocketing on a train in Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They charged me with that, but they never proved that. I didn't have a ticket. Please just tell me if they have managed to prove anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you not convicted for one year and three years on probation?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they worked the same way as those people in Omarska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the Croats worked the same way as the Serbs did?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you know who were members of the police in Zagreb and the former Yugoslavia. You are trying now to present the wrong picture here in court.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the judge in Zagreb also Serb?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He probably was or maybe he wasn't, but it was the police who played the major role there. Never in my life has a single criminal offence been proved against me. And they always tried to accuse me of being a thief, a criminal, because actually I was against the system which was in place at that time. Please, do not bring up things that have never been proved against me. We are here to try war crimes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, let me interrupt you once again. You're not here to argue with the counsel and the counsel is not here to argue with you. You are here to answer questions in a clear manner, in a precise manner, concisely and clearly. And you have to concentrate yourself to the questions put to you by the Defence counsel. You have to understand that the counsel has the right to conduct a cross-examination of you as a witness about what you told to Ms. Hollis, and he also has the right to cross-examine you on your credibility. The Defence counsel will continue with his questions and please answer with yes, no, or I don't know. Otherwise, we will never finish. And let me also remind Mr. Simic to ask questions in a concise and precise manner and try to obtain answers in this way. And please, try to avoid arguing with the witness. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Beganovic, were you tried and convicted in Novi Sad for the criminal offence of bribery of an official and authorised individual in order to engage in illegal activity?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I was first released, then the policeman was to be punished. And then in the end, to avoid punishing the policeman, they punished me. These are all put up affairs, this whole biography is a fabrication by the Prijedor SUP to give the impression that I was a criminal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, the answer should be yes or no. Were you convicted?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is sufficient as an answer. Continue, Mr. Simic.

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why don't you list everything that you have and I will say immediately that I was convicted and that will speed everything up. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you convicted in the District Court in Banja Luka as well for a very serious traffic offence of driving under conditions of inebriation, very heavy alcoholism?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now that you have admitted to things that you did not mention before, let us go through the whole list quickly and you can tell me yes or no.

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Pickpocketing in Prijedor; eight months of imprisonment, two years probation.

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Third Municipal Court in Prijedor; for concealing and handling stolen goods, a fine of 2.000 dinars.

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Municipal Court in Zagreb, pickpocketing; one year imprisonment, three years on probation.

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ruling of the District Court in Banja Luka, one year in prison and seizure of a driving license, confiscation of a driving license. Decision of the Municipal Court in Novi Sad; seven months of imprisonment, three years on probation.

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Beganovic.

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was such a criminal, how come I never went to prison? I always got these probational sentences.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, leave it to the Judges to make their own conclusions. You provide the information. The Tribunal is here to make the conclusions. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are any proceedings being conducted against you in Prijedor in connection with events that took place a couple of months ago?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A couple of months ago? What on earth could that be? How do I know? I was in Prijedor as a tourist a couple of months ago, and that's all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you went there as a tourist a couple of months ago, did an incident occur?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it did, and I reported it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of incident?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Verbal and physical -- I was physically attacked in Prijedor, on the road. On the Prijedor-to-Sanski Most road, at Tukovi, I was physically attacked. I have witnesses of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll come back to that. That's all for the moment. Thank you. Mr. Beganovic, I should like to speed things up a little, move forward, linked to some of your testimony yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Simic, please speed things up because we have spent almost 40 minutes talking about weapons and the legal position of the witness. We've been talking only about those weapons and the record of the witness. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] I accept part of the blame, but I think Mr. Beganovic shares that blame with me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday you said that when the first 1.200 German marks were taken from you when you went to the toilet, by people from Banja Luka, you said that this policeman said to you when he took those 1.200 German marks from you, "If you tell anyone, I'll kill you."

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what he said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. How can you explain, and you have repeated several times, that everything could be done in public, without concealing what they were doing?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why, then, would he say, "If you tell anyone, I'll kill you"? He said that I shouldn't tell anyone in case his superiors might take the money away from him. They had to carry that money to them. The lower level people had to hand over money to those higher up, and these sitting here had to pass it on to Milan Andzic and to others above them. So Brk carried the money to Milan Andzic; they were working for him. This is common knowledge. Everyone knew about that in Omarska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm afraid the witness is responding in the old way.

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I have to explain because you asked me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Beganovic, in your earlier statements, I see -- and I think there is a technical error there -- that in your statements, the date of the takeover has been confused with the day of the military counterattack on Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand what you mean by "counterattack".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll come to that. Were there any armed operations on the 30th of April?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, they barged in, masked, under weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a conflict?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How do I know? I wasn't in that part of town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Correct. On the 30th of May, when an attempt was made at a counterattack, you used the term "if it took place at all," and you said that you were listening to the radio, together with Kapetanovic, at Dr. Sadikovic's house, and that the radio was giving instructions as to how you should behave.

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any reports as to what had happened during the night in the town of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What had happened the previous night?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That same night, yes.

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How do I know what happened when I ended up in the camp?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Beganovic, my question is very clear: In the course of the night of the 30th of May, early in the morning prior to your arrest, or a couple of hours, five or six hours, was there a very fierce armed conflict in Prijedor? Did the radio report about that?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't hear any reports on the radio, nor did I know that there was a conflict. I just saw a large number of Serb troops in my area; that's all I saw. And that is what I said in my statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that night you didn't hear any armed conflict?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean "armed conflict"? What sort of armed conflict? Are you saying --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Simic, you asked whether there was an armed conflict in the night of the 30th of May. The witness has said that he didn't know. Don't insist on that, please. Otherwise we'll never make any progress. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The radio reported on the death of 15 or 16 Serb policemen.

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They would report on Serb deaths on the radio in Croatia. What do I care about Serb deaths, deaths of terrorists who went to Croatia to loot there? They came back with a booty and then he got killed. What do I care? Let them all get killed in that way, to fight like that and go to war like that, in the interests of booty. And that is a JNA army. It's a looting war. Don't ask me these things, whether I cared about 16 thieves getting killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear the news that 16 people got killed?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not, nor did I listen to any such news.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Beganovic, let us go back to the event that we're most concerned with, and that is this second beating by Nikica Janjic.

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me first try and establish when this happened.

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean at what time?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the date?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Slowly. Let me ask the questions.

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hurry things up a little because of the Judges.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us roughly the date, not the time, when this occurred.

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can tell you roughly that it was in mid-June. That is a very rough, approximate, date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have to go back to your statement yesterday and your testimony in the Tadic trial. That evening, did you spend the night in the big room next to the restaurant?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Behind the restaurant, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We know what we're talking about. Fine. Did you, after that, spend a few nights somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was returned to the pista the next day, the next morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How much time did you spend at the pista?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 10 days, 10 or 12, 10 or 11.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fine. After the first beating, you spent two nights in the "white house".

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: According to a reconstruction of the events. Then you were returned to the pista, according to your statement.

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, briefly, and then I went back to number 15.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You went back to number 15. In your signed statement, you said that this second beating occurred a couple of days prior to St. Peter's Day.

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether it was Peter's Day. It was some sort of a festivity. It may have been some other holiday which they celebrated by setting fire to people and throwing them into wells.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We're talking about this particular event. Did it occur a couple of days prior to those fires and burnings that you're talking about?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was on that same day. No, actually, two or three days before that, this second beating. Two or three days before, tyres were set on fire and people were thrown into the wells.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please tell me clearly that the second beating by Janjic took place a couple of days before the bonfires?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, maybe two days before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday in your testimony, you described Mr. Kvocka as almost a friend --

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, my mother was a close friend with his mother-in-law. That is what I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, that is how I understood you. Did you know Mr. Kvocka personally?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew him from town, yes. I would never socialise with anyone like that. You expect me to be friends with such a person?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Beganovic --

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The communists made people like that, people like he was, criminals.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me quote from your statement, given two years after the event. So I assume your memory was fresher then than it is today, and I quote: "With Drago Prcac, a Serb shift leader, shift commander, who replaced somebody whom other people called Kvocka ..." Mr. Beganovic, does that describe somebody you knew so well, by saying that "other people called Kvocka" rather than saying "Miroslav Kvocka" or simply "Policeman Kvocka"? Please don't ask me anything. I am the one asking the questions.

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There may be a technical mistake in the translation when I said "other people called Kvocka." Everybody called him Kvocka. Why would I say that? Is that how you want to save him? MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Beganovic, we're talking about the second beating prior to St. Peter's Day. Why did you seek assistance from Mr. Kvocka, in view of your family links between your mother and his mother-in-law and the fact that he brought food to your mother? Why didn't you ask him for assistance?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How could I ask for assistance from somebody who wanted to throw my body into the pit? Who ever was given any assistance by him in Omarska. You want an answer? That is your answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question is: Did you know that he wrote that down before that?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not before Nikica told me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why didn't you ask for his assistance before that?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both he and Ckalja were at the entrance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you contact with him?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He did his part, he said where I should go and he went off, probably not to be on the spot when these things happened. He knew what he was doing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Beganovic, he had to write it down, Emir Beganovic. He could have simply given orders.

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How did he know that there would be a trial? Maybe I made the whole thing up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why would anyone write that down when he could have said it?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Your Honours, for the interpretation, this is quite impossible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have to intervene. You know that we have interpreters here. It is impossible, Witness, to follow. You have to slow down. You have to make breaks between the questions and the answers. And I have to remind Mr. Simic once again: Ask questions. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I am trying to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Simic. I'm having difficulty following the line of your cross-examination, because it seems to me that you keep asking the witness why somebody else is doing something. And since he probably has no idea why a third party would be doing something, and that's not within the scope of what he knows, it sounds to me like you're making an argument that may more properly be made at the time when you make your closing argument, or at least I'm having difficulty figuring out what you want him to say about somebody else's reasons for doing something. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is exactly why I really have to ask you once again to try and ask questions, questions which go to the knowledge of the witness. Because if you ask the witness why a third person did something or thought something, we will never finish, Mr. Simic. You know that. Please, go directly to the matter and ask specific questions to which he can provide answers. Otherwise we will enter into a debate and we are not here to debate or to argue. We're not here to make allegations but to obtain information and the allegations, and submissions will follow after that. So would you please, all of you, bear in mind a very simple rule of direct examination and cross-examination. The rule of three C's: Clear, concrete, and concise. Please, ask clear and specific questions to which the witness can provide answers because of his knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if the Prosecution could just make a simple procedural request at this point. It would assist the Prosecution if, when counsel is referring to a statement or the transcript, if they would note what page of the statement they're referring to. That way it would be easier for us to find what they are referring to.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters have not been provided with the relevant statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Simic. Would it be possible for you to tell the Judges and the Prosecution counsel the page, the number of the page of the document you're referring to so that we can follow. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I think I will be able to do that, and I will soon finish the examination.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Beganovic, the note which was shown to you by late Nikica Janjic, was that note a death sentence for you?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Beganovic, in your statement on page 12, the statement you gave to the investigators, you did not mention that -- how come that you didn't mention not one single time on those 22 pages such a significant event that -- namely that a death sentence was imposed to you while you were in Omarska? I'm referring to your statement given in 1994 and in the beginning of 1995, the statements in which you did not mention this fact. You did not mention such an important event as a death sentence?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, of course it was a death sentence. My corpse was supposed to be thrown in pit number two. Why was I supposed to state that? It was a normal thing. I was sentenced to that in Omarska at least 100 times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want an answer, Witness.

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I told you. You didn't ask me a specific question. When you ask me specific questions, I will give you specific answers. Please, do not try to be philosophical here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this statement which consists of 22 pages, you spoke in some detail, not prompted with questions --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Simic, the witness has told you that it was implicit in the statement. I think you should have asked the question in a different way. You should have ask asked the

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: And the witness actually told you that the death sentence was implicit. So you have the answer. Please, do not insist. Go on to another question, Mr. Simic. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Beganovic, I am now referring to your testimony given to the Trial Chamber seized of the Tadic case, page 117. Why didn't you at that time, in any way, mention the note that you spoke about yesterday, the note that you described as your death sentence?

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: The case in question was the Tadic case, not the Kvocka case, and I was asked some other questions. I'm not the person asking questions. I'm only here to give answers. And I give answers to the questions that are put to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the following page, Mr. Beganovic, page 118, you talk about Ckalja and you also talk about Kvocka and this was still during the Tadic case?

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: Well, this all depended on the questions. I provided answers to certain questions. I actually don't understand what you want to know. It's as if you were speaking Japanese to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm being very clear, Mr. Beganovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Simic, the witness has given his answer. He said that his answers depended on the questions that were asked at that time. Please, do not insist. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I should like to finish with the following matter. I will now quote from page 125 of the Tadic transcript. Mr. Beganovic, at that time during the identification of Mr. Tadic, did you say -- did you refer to him as Serb garbage?

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: Yes, I did. Did I offend him, by any chance, by saying that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: I'm just trying to understand the answer. When you say "refer to", "Did you refer to him as Serb garbage," do you mean Tadic or Kvocka? It's not clear. Tadic or -- MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] To Mr. Tadic, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And my last question for you, again, page 138 of the transcript. At one point you said, "What they ate. What do I know what those scum ate? Pork, must be." Did you state that in the Tadic case?

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I did. They ate pork and they drank brandy and then they would go crazy in the sun and the heat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, Mr. Simic has simply asked you whether you indeed stated that in the Tadic case or not. If it's enough to say yes, you should stop at that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour. Yes, I did. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And two last questions. Mr. Beganovic, while you were testifying here yesterday, while you were sitting here, did you at one point turn to Mr. Radic, and I have to apologise in advance to this Honourable Chamber and the ladies present in the courtroom, did you call him a motherfucker?

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: Me, no. Who heard that? Who saw that? No, it's not true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Beganovic, my last question. When Mr. Kvocka noticed that and when he asked Radic whether he, too, had seen it, didn't you again, I have to apologise once again, Your Honours, didn't you say again to all of them, "You're all motherfuckers"?

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: No, I didn't. I didn't. I didn't say that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Beganovic.

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: Thank you too. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] I have concluded my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Simic. Now, we will move onto the cross-examination which will be conducted by Mr. Stojanovic in accordance with the order which was indicated to us yesterday. Mr. Stojanovic, could you perhaps come here as well, because otherwise you will be speaking behind the witness' back.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think I will be very brief, so I don't think it would really be necessary. I should like to try and to lower the tension a little bit which has -- was the result of this previous cross-examination. The Defence of Mr. Zigic has decided not to ask any questions of Mr. Beganovic. We know from the Tadic case that Mr. Beganovic suffered a lot in Omarska. Regardless or not withstanding other circumstances and other consequences which the Judges will be able to appraise, we can only express our regret.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Stojanovic, this is not a moment for that. Would you just tell us whether you have any questions for this witness or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, we don't, Your Honour. By what I have said I do not wish to cause any prejudice to anybody else from -- anybody else in this group, any other of the accused, so we do not have any questions. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Stojanovic. I see that Mr. O'Sullivan will now take the floor instead of Mr. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: May I be allowed to take a document from the Prosecution? May I be allowed to step across the floor before I step to the podium? May it please the Court. Cross-examined by Mr. O'Sullivan:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Beganovic, we've already established that you met with the Office of the Prosecutor in December 1994 and January 1995; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: With the assistance of the usher, can I ask that a copy of that statement be provided to the witness. I also have a copy for Your Honours if you would like to see it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Exhibit D1/2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you have two documents in front of you. One document is in English and one document is in Bosnian. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: Yes, I can see them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I've given you the Bosnian version so you can follow more easily my questions, all right? Did you hear me? Yes? Did you hear me?

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I must explain that you have -- I'm holding in my hand the English version which is redacted. You have an -- the English version -- do you see the English version?

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: This is the English one?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yours is not redacted in English. Do you see that? There are no black marks on your English copy.

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I must explain that the document that I received from the Prosecution just now is the unredacted version which I have before the witness. I apologise for giving you a copy of the redacted version. That's the only one I had in my files. We can certainly provide you with the unredacted version as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The reason it was redacted, Mr. Beganovic, was for your protection initially. I'm going to ask you to look at the front page of your statement.

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: In Bosnian?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If it's more convenient for you, yes.

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Across the top you see is written "International Tribunal for the Former Yugoslavia"; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And below that it says "witness statement"?

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And further down on that first page, you see the dates of the interview?

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at the bottom of the first page is your signature; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: Not here on the Bosnian version; however, on the English one, yes, it is there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if you look -- if you flip through the English version, at the bottom of each page is your initial; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sticking with the English version, can you turn to the last page, please.

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You may also have to turn to the last page of the Bosnian version. It's written "witness acknowledgement" on the last page.

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in the English version you'll see it's dated 19/1/95. Correct?

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You signed that acknowledgement on that date. Correct?

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you signed the acknowledgement, you confirmed that you made a voluntary, truthful statement; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we go back to the front page for a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: Of the English version?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Either one. You met with the investigators over a period of four days, correct? 14 December, 1994; 18, 19 January, 1995?

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the first date, December 14th, approximately how long did you meet with the investigators? All day?

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: Can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say it was a normal eight-hour day? Would you accept that?

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: Maybe with interruptions. It was a long time ago. I really can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the second day, December 15th, would you accept that it was similar to the first, a normal working day with breaks?

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: I really can't say for sure. I know I cooperated. I know there were breaks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the third day, the 18th of January? Would you say that it was a normal working day with the investigators, with regular breaks?

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does the same hold true for the fourth day?

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: Probably. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The front page indicates you were interviewed by three people, that's directly below the dates of the interview. A person named McIntosh, Edgerton, and Blaxill. Is that how you remember it, three people?

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I take it they proceeded by way of question and answer with you?

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there was no pressure put on you to make the statement, was there?

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You spoke freely?

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were not hurried by these people to make your statement, were you?

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: No, nobody hurried me. In an investigation like any other investigation, it went its course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And clearly you made this statement approximately two years after the relevant events.

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So these events were still very fresh in your mind?

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: Roughly so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would you accept that you gave the best account of the important events, places, and people?

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: I did my best to be as clear as possible. To answer the questions put to me in the clearest possible manner, to tell the investigators how things happened. So I did my very best. I sought to be as clear and precise as possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And complete.

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because you knew this document would be used, or your statement would be used in trial proceedings.

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: I didn't know at the time whether it would be used. I assumed that perhaps one day -- since the investigators did appear that they were working on something -- that one day, whether it would be in five, ten, or twenty years, I didn't know at the time, these people would be brought to trial.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I realise it's been a while. But let me remind you of the acknowledgement at the end of this document, and it says, "I am aware that it," the statement, "may be used in legal proceedings before the International Tribunal." So you would agree with me that you were aware of that. Just to remind you.

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I was aware, but I didn't know when the trial would take place. But I agreed to testify and express my willingness to testify.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand. Now, Mr. Beganovic, no where in your statement do you mention the name Krle, do you?

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: When they asked me, they put me a question in connection with Krle, I gave them an answer. If you ask me about Kvocka, I can't tell you about Krle. That's how it was in the investigation. That is how I behaved. I answered the questions put to me, depending on the interests of the investigators. I didn't know what they were interested in, whether it was Kvocka or Dusko Tadic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please listen to my question and answer it, all right? No where in your statement do you mention the name Krle. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't remember. But if you say I didn't, then I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You accept you didn't?

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: If it's not in the statement -- I don't know my statement by heart -- but if it's not in the statement, then I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I ask you to turn to page 17 of the Bosnian version, which is page 18 of the English version.

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: Which page?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Page 17 in the Bosnian version.

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which is page 18 in the English version, for those following in English. On this page, you talk about the person Brk trying to extort money from you to be freed. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, Mr. O'Sullivan. Perhaps it would be useful to refer to the specific paragraph so as to make it easier for us to find the quotation.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Yes. In the English version, it's the third paragraph, which is the longest paragraph, five lines up, and in the Bosnian version, it's the second paragraph, at the end.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you found that, Mr. Beganovic?

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: You're referring to Brk, what I said about Brk? Yes, I've found it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good. There you talk about Brk trying to extort money from you for your freedom; correct?

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You make no mention of Krle there, do you? Correct?

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: Probably nobody asked me who else was there. I always said that Krle was there in that group of men. I didn't have any direct contact with Krle. He was standing there, and I can't remember who else was there. I know Brk was there, Krle, and another guard. And as Brk spoke to me, I conversed with him and negotiated with him whether I would be transferred or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you told the truth when you made this statement, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: The truth, of course. Everything is the truth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you testified in Tadic, you told the truth.

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You never mentioned Krle in Tadic, did you?

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: I didn't mention him because no one asked me about him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You gave a complete account of events in your statement here, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: As complete as the investigators were interested in. I could talk about Omarska for years and still it wouldn't be complete without mentioning all the criminals and what they did in Omarska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My point is this, Mr. Beganovic: When events are fresh in your mind two years later, you don't mention Krle. You don't mention it in Tadic. Do you expect us to believe that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, Mr. O'Sullivan. The witness has already given you a reply. He said that his answers corresponded to the investigator's questions. I'm sorry. Please move on to another question.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. O'Sullivan. Mr. Fila, it is your turn. I don't know whether we should make the break. We have seven minutes to go to the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It will not be sufficient.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In that case, perhaps we should have the break now and resume with your cross-examination. We will now have a 30-minute break.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps Mr. Simic could finish in those few minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Oh, yes. Very well. Thank you very much for your suggestion. Mr. Jovan Simic is now going to cross-examine you. He is the Defence counsel of Mr. Prcac, and you are going to answer his questions, please. You have the floor, Mr. Jovan Simic. MR. J. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Cross-examined by Mr. J. Simic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Beganovic, you stated yesterday that you didn't know Mr. Prcac; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said yesterday that you don't even know his first name, whether it's Dragoljub or Dragan.

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: We called him Drago in the camp, Drago Prcac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you didn't know his real name, his proper name, his first name.

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned Mr. Prcac twice. Both times you said that this was not something that you knew yourself but that you had heard from others. Is that correct? Do you have any direct knowledge about Mr. Prcac?

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. J. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have no further questions. But I should like to appeal to the Chamber that this is not direct knowledge or any kind of evidence, so that in the opinion of the Defence, this evidence is irrelevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we heard the witness, Mr. Simic. Thank you very much, Mr. Jovan Simic. I think five minutes is certainly not enough for Mr. Fila, so we're going to have a half-hour break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You may be seated. We are now going to resume our hearing, as soon as the witness is brought back to the courtroom. Mr. O'Sullivan.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Yes. I must beg your indulgence for an oversight on my part. Defence Exhibit D1/2 was marked for identification but I did not tender it into evidence. I'd like to do that at this time, please. I ask that that exhibit be part of the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Hollis, any objections?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps I should make a suggestion here. At the end of the testimony, we could perhaps deal with all of the exhibits that have been used during the testimony, instead of dealing with them on an individual basis. This applies both to the Prosecution and the Defence. So at the end of the testimony, we will deal with the exhibits altogether. I think this is much better than proceeding on a case-by-case basis. Are we ready to continue? Witness, you are now going to answer questions that will be put to you by Mr. Fila, who is representing Mr. Radic in this case. Mr. Fila, you have the floor. Cross-examined by Mr. Fila:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Beganovic, I know that you have suffered a lot, but I have to ask you a few questions and I hope I will not cause you any pain by my questions. First of all, let me ask you, in your statement, the one that you had before you a moment ago, and during your testimony in the Tadic case, why didn't you mention Krkan?

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: No such question was ever put to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, then. You said the same thing in response to a previous question, and I'm satisfied with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's very good, Mr. Fila. You did not insist on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I assume that you didn't know Mr. Krkan prior to your arrival here.

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you first learn that his name was Krkan, or Mladjo Radic?

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: In the camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you learned both his name and his nickname.

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So while you were giving your statement to the investigators, you knew about his name.

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise to the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In answering questions that were put to you by Ms. Hollis, you mentioned that you had seen him pass by the restaurant a few times.

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you saw him in a kind of a glass house.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, let me just state that at that moment the witness did not indicate the precise location of the glass house. So I should like to ask the witness to do it now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us exactly what location exactly you had in mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Usher, could you please help the witness to approach the model so that he can answer the question put to him by Mr. Fila.

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: It was in this area here [indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, then. What was he doing there when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: He was getting in. He was climbing down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that, but you said that he stood there for a while.

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: Well, yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was he doing? Was he standing guard or something?

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: No, I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, we won't argue about that. You don't know what he was doing and that's enough. You said that he was armed with an automatic rifle at that time.

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you observe in what way people were armed? I'm referring only to the guards.

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: Yes, I could observe that. Most of them had automatic weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The same as Mladjo Radic, or were there any others who were armed with different kinds of weapons?

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: Yes, there were other types of weapons as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Fila, sorry to interrupt you, but maybe the witness could resume his seat if you don't need him near the model anymore. Witness, you may take your seat. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I'm here referring to the police and the guards. I'm not interested in visitors such as Zigic, for example. You said yesterday that Mr. Kvocka had a pump-action rifle?

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He had the same kind of weapon as Mladjo Radic.

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone else have any different kind of weapon?

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: Well, I couldn't tell you about that. In most of the cases they had automatic rifles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just like Mladjo Radic.

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: Yes, mostly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly yesterday -- and I do not intend to argue about it, I just want to check whether I understood you correctly -- while you were in room 15, you were unable to observe what was going on outside.

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Mujo's room?

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: While I was in Mujo's room, I would venture outside from time to time, so I would sit near the wall of the building and I could see what was happening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But while you were at the pista, you could observe what was happening.

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Beganovic, let me state once again I fully understand what you were going through. I know you were not on a vacation in Hawaii. However, I have to ask you my questions. As regards the two months and six days, more or less, how much time did you spend on the pista?

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: Between 10 and 12 days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So can we say that your testimony, in respect of Mladjo Radic, Krkan, concerns that period of time? Was it during that period of time that you occasionally saw him?

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: I think I saw him more often later on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: Well, when we would go out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but that would have been in the area which you indicated for us. You're referring to the area that you indicated on the model.

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: Yes, the area in the vicinity of the restaurant, from this side of the table.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, then. So I did understand you correctly. You spoke about the guard named Pavlovic.

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's a bit difficult for me to ask this question, but how did he receive you? Did he take your identity card? How did this go?

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: Well, he approached me when he saw those crackers that I had at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But he applied the same procedure to other people before you and after you.

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: Yes, he was taking down the necessary information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your personal details, you mean. So because of those fire crackers, I don't know what he thought of them, but he stopped. And did anyone else resume the making of the list?

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: Well, not in the case of myself personally, except for Koka, who was making a list while I was sitting in front of the "white house". So it was more than a month later that I was registered again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know Omarska while it was still a mine?

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: Yes, I did know Omarska, but I never visited the area comprising the hangar, the restaurant, and other locations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned the living conditions there which were inhumane, and I, of course, grant you that, I agree with you.

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: They were not only inhumane but --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but this is the description in the status. Was it possible for you to obtain any water? Was there a tap of some sort?

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: Yes, there was a tap. There were several taps in room number 15, and also in Mujo's room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the water was the water from the tap. There was no other special water that was brought to you from elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who prepared the food?

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And my last question. You stated that you were exchanged. You were exchanged for whom?

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: For some Serb civilians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who were where?

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: Who were on the other side in Brcko Gradiska. I don't know. I just passed by in the exchange.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they also detainees like you?

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know?

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: Well, I know because people told us that. We stood there for about an hour. They were probably civilians who wanted to move from that territory and we were exchanged for them. They were mainly women, children, elderly people over the age of 60. As for my group, nobody was older than 40 years of age.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did they have to be exchanged? Why weren't they simply let go?

utterances.speaker: "Why didn't you mention this fact?"
utterances.text: Well, you know what kind of war it was. You know that all three national sides pursue the same kind of policy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I agree with you on that. Let me finish with a question that I hope you will answer truthfully.
