utterances.text: What happened after that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: He grabbed me by the shoulder and he threw me out of the hotel, together with Muharem Murselovic, and he took us to the bus.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "he" threw you out of the hotel, who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: To Ranko Vujasinovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is his ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: He was a Serb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your friend the doctor, what was his ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: He was a Serb too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned that a person named Ritan intervened. What was Ritan's ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Serb.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could we ask the witness to speak into the microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, once you were pushed toward the bus, did you then get onto the bus?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Ranko told the driver to open the door and to drive off this scum, and then he kicked me in the behind once again. We got on the bus and the bus started off towards Luka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, where did the bus go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: To the MUP. Sorry, to the MUP. MUP or SUP, that's where it stopped.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you arrived at the SUP, what did you observe there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: The bus stopped. Muharem Murselovic got off the bus because he saw Milutin Cado, a police commander, and he wanted to address him, to ask him something. I don't know what.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you observe then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Muharem came back to the bus and the officer asked him, "What are you doing?" and he said, "I saw the commander and I wanted to talk to him." And he asked him what ethnic group he was and what his name was. He said Murselovic. Then again he cursed his mother and he said he would kill us all and that we should get on the bus and lie down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Murselovic, what was his ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: He was a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, after you went to the SUP, where did you go from there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: We went to Tomasica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And from Tomasica, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Omarska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what time of the day, if you remember, did you arrive at Omarska?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Around 4.00 or 5.00, or maybe 6.00, 5.00 or 6.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The people that were on your bus with you, the other people that had been arrested and put on your bus, did you recognise any of those people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the people that you recognised, what was their ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you arrived at Omarska camp, where did the bus stop?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: At the pista.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened then, after your bus stopped on the pista?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: We got off the bus and we stood in front of the building that used to be a restaurant. We had to put our hands against the wall. We were searched and beaten.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, these people that searched you and beat you after you got off the bus, how often after that, if ever, did you see any of those people in Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: I would see them but I could no longer remember those people anymore.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, after you were searched and you were beaten, then where did you go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: We entered a large hall, a large premise, and we were there. We were in that hall until the 6th or 7th of August, or the 6th, I think it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you refer to a hall, in what building are you talking about the hall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Where the restaurant was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This hall that you were in, did it come to be known by a particular name or by a particular reference?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Well, they called it Mujo's room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you indicated that you were held in Mujo's room until approximately the 6th of August. While you were held in Mujo's room, were you in Mujo's room 24 hours a day, or were you also in other areas?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: I was also in other areas; at the pista, in the "white house", in the garage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if we take those in turn, when you were in the "white house", how --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Restaurant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were in the "white house", how long were you in the "white house"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: I was there for three days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you were on the pista. How long were you on the pista?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: I was on the pista for some 10 or 12 days. We were coming and going.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Coming and going from where?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: From Mujo's room to the pista.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also mentioned being in a place you called the garage. Now, in what building was that garage located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Where the restaurant is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long were you in the garage?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Three days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were in Omarska camp, were you ever interrogated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you interrogated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Upstairs, on the floor, on the first floor of the restaurant building.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this time if I could ask that the witness approach the model and point to the various areas he has described.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but Mr. President, to do so we must go into closed session because of image distortion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So we're going into closed session now.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can forego that with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Madam Hollis, because going into closed session is always an exception to the public character of the hearings. Perhaps the witness could give a detailed description; that will take a little more time, but we will be respecting the principle of a public hearing. Thank you, Ms. Hollis.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness AJ, when you talk about this room or this area you called the garage, as you are seated and you look at the building directly ahead of you, to your right, not the long building but the smaller red building, how do you refer to that building? What building is that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, Madam Hollis. Couldn't we use this exhibit on the ELMO, perhaps?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Once he identifies the building, yes, Your Honour, I believe we could.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So as you are looking to the smaller red building on your right, what is that building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: The first black door on the right-hand side, that is the garage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you call the building that you are referring to here? What building is that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: The restaurant. The restaurant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So as you look at that building, there is a black door on the right, and that's the door you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: The garage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's on the very corner of the building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, when did you leave Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: On the 6th of August.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the time that you were in Omarska camp, did you recognise any camp personnel as people you had known before the camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell the Court the names or nicknames of some of the people that you recognised.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Well, I recognised Krkan, Kvocka, Prcac -- Kvocka, Prcac. I can't remember now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: I know them all, because all of them had their haircuts in my place, shaved, had drinks and had coffee, and they all know me well too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let's take those, if we can, in order. You mentioned that before the camp you knew a person you called Krkan. Now, to your knowledge, is that a proper name, "Krkan"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know Krkan's --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Mladjo Radic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before going to the camp, how long would you say you had known him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: I had known him some 15 years, 10 or 15 years at least.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also mentioned a person you called Kvocka. Prior to you going to the camp, how long had you known him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: For a long time as well, because I had this shop for a long time, and I would see them on the road, in MUP. I was quite free, I moved around freely, so we knew each other.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Kvocka, was Kvocka married?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the ethnicity of his wife?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know his wife's father's last name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Crnalic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you also mentioned Prcac. How long had you known Prcac before you were in the camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Also for a long time. A long time. About 15, or maybe 20 years, or 10. Between 10 and 20.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to ask you a few questions about each one of these individuals. As to Krkan, while you were in Omarska, during what period of time did you see him in the camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: I would see him sometimes every day, every other day. It depended on when I went out and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During what time period? You went to the camp on the 30th of May; you indicated you left the camp in early August. During that time, was there a particular time period that you saw him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Perhaps two or three days would go by for me not to see him. Maybe five.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you saw Krkan, what would Krkan be doing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Standing, walking.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you see him in the camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: I would see him in front of the building, of the restaurant, behind the restaurant. There wasn't a fixed position.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see him enter any of the buildings in the camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you saw him, what weapons, if any, would he have?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: They had Kalashnikovs and that sort of thing, short weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness AJ, I would specifically like to ask about Krkan. If you remember the times you saw Krkan, what kinds of weapons, if any, would he have?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: A Kalashnikov. I don't know how they called it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, for Kvocka, during what period of time did you see Kvocka in the camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Maybe some 20 days to one month.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During this 20 days to one month that you saw him in the camp, how often would you see him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: We would sometimes see him every day, every other day, every third day. It depended.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you saw him, what would he be doing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Walking around, around the compound.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "around the compound," what areas of the camp are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Around the pista. He had an office inside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He had an office inside what building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: The restaurant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the time you saw him, what weapons, if any, did he have?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: He had a rifle, a pump-action gun.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, regarding Prcac, during what period of time did you see him in Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Well, he may have come after some 20 days or a month; that is, after I had been there for that long.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After Prcac came to the camp, how often did you see him in the camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: I would see him like that the same, once a day, sometimes twice, three times. Once I even talked to him. It depended on where I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where was it in the camp that you would see him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: In front of the building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: The restaurant building. On this side. The middle black door, the black door in the middle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you speak about this side, are you talking about the portion of the restaurant building that is facing toward you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The portion that is furthest away from the Judges?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you talk about the black door in the middle, are you talking about a black door in the middle of this back part of the building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: In the middle. In the middle. In front of the pista here and there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you say "here and there", what other areas, other than the one you have just identified, what other areas did you see Prcac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Between the hangar and the main entrance, the hangar on the left and the main entrance, because I was also on the pista.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that area between the hangar and the restaurant building you're referring to as the pista?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Yeah. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On those occasions when you saw Prcac, what would he be doing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: I don't know what his job was, nor what he was doing. He walked around. He went in and out. What he did, what duties he had.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What building or buildings did you see him go into and out of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Well, mostly through the main entrance of the building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of what building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: This one on the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that is, please --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Restaurant, the restaurant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that the only building you saw him go into and out of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: That is all I saw, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The times that you saw Prcac, what weapons, if any, did he have?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean you didn't --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, this might be a convenient place to break the examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Madam Hollis. Yes, we agree that this is a good time for the break or rather for us to adjourn for today. Witness, you're going to come back tomorrow, tomorrow at 9.30 -- no, no, I'm sorry. The working rhythm is such that one forgets that we are entitled to a weekend after all. So in fact, it's Monday.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we're available tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe we can organise it if the Defence feels like it. We have the witness. I will be here. We can talk about it for a next time. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] We're ready too.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think we are simply attempting to say that we are very flexible to assist you in expediting the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you repeat?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I think we were just saying we would be happy to help in expediting the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are risking the possibility of the Chamber accepting.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: We encourage that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think there is a lot of people who need the weekend and I think we need it too. So we can have a rest for the weekend. And perhaps speed up things a little more during the week, not to waste time during working hours, have a good rest so as to gain in speed when we come back. That way, you will not be running the risk, but don't repeat yourself too often because we could reorganise ourselves. Anyway, have a good weekend, everyone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: at 2.35 p.m., to be reconvened on Monday the 8th day of May, 2000, at 9.30 a.m. 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
